headline: Large Energy Users Pay Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill mandates that large energy users, such as data centers, bear the costs of new transmission infrastructure built specifically for their facilities, rather than socializing these costs across all ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Governor Abigail Spanberger, State Corporation Commission (SCC), Virginia families, small businesses, residential ratepayers, environmental groups, some state senators.
news_headline: SCC Requires Data Centers to Pay for New Transmission Infrastructure
news_summary: The State Corporation Commission (SCC), following Governor Spanberger's urging, ordered data centers to cover the cost of transmission infrastructure built exclusively for their facilities, saving Virginia families and small businesses hundreds of millions of dollars. This decision ensures large energy users pay their full share for grid upgrades, rather than shifting costs to residential ratepayers.

headline: Data Centers Report Water Use
short_summary: This bill mandates waterworks operators to categorize and report the total volume of water provided to data centers, increasing transparency regarding the industry's water consumption.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: State Sen. Kannan Srinivasan (D-Loudoun), Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ), environmental groups, communities concerned about water resources.
opponents: Data center industry (potential, for increased scrutiny).
news_headline: New regulations beef up data centers' required water use reporting in Virginia
news_summary: New regulations, effective January 2027, will require waterworks operators to categorize monthly water sales data, including usage by data centers, to provide more transparency on water consumption. This bill aims to fill a data gap and aid the DEQ in water supply planning, especially during droughts.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Regulations
short_summary: This bill requires new high-energy-use facilities, primarily data centers, to conduct site assessments for noise impact on nearby residential areas and schools before local approval, and allows localities to examine other environmental and agricultural impacts, having been approved by the Governor.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local residents, communities concerned about noise pollution and environmental impact, local governments.
news_headline: Data center noise irks Virginia neighbors: 'You just want to curse'
news_summary: Residents in Virginia's "Data Center Alley" are increasingly complaining about constant, high-pitched noise and fumes from nearby data centers, especially when backup generators run during power failures. This has led to calls for stricter noise ordinances and greater accountability for industrial noise impacting residential neighborhoods.
